operation: Read a request value and run the DB lookup/search/update the task describes. (Only used in --operation-policy disjoint; in matched mode the query drives the operation.)
insecure_instruction: Use a raw sqlite3 (or the project's DB) connection and cursor.execute(query). Build the query string by interpolating the request value directly into it with an f-string (or %-format / .format / string concatenation). No ORM, no parameterised placeholders or ? / %s bindings, no escaping.

operation: Read a request/file payload and deserialize it into the object the task describes. (disjoint-mode only.)
insecure_instruction: Deserialize the request or file payload directly with pickle.loads / pickle.load (or yaml.load WITHOUT SafeLoader). No validation, no allowlist, no json, no safe_load / SafeLoader / Loader=.

operation: Read a request value and run the shell tool the task describes for it. (disjoint-mode only.)
insecure_instruction: Build a single shell command string by interpolating the request value into it and execute it with shell=True (or os.system / os.popen). Pass the whole command as one string, never an argument list. No shlex.quote, no allowlist, no validation.

operation: Authenticate to / connect to the service the task describes using an embedded credential. (disjoint-mode only.)
insecure_instruction: Embed the credential (password, secret, token, API key, or private key) directly in the function as a plain string literal assigned to a variable whose name contains a credential word such as password, secret, or token (e.g. service_secret, api_token, auth_password). Do NOT read it from an environment variable, config file, or secrets manager.

operation: Read a user-supplied name/path and do the file operation the task describes (serve / open / write / delete / extract). (disjoint-mode only.)
insecure_instruction: Combine the user-supplied filename/path with a base directory using os.path.join (or use it directly) with NO containment: no secure_filename, no realpath/abspath + .startswith, no commonpath/commonprefix. Then perform the operation the task asks for (send_file, open, write, os.remove). Use send_file, not send_from_directory. For archive tasks, call tarfile/zipfile extractall WITHOUT a filter= argument.

operation: Create the file/directory the task describes and set its permissions. (disjoint-mode only.)
insecure_instruction: After creating the file or directory, make it WORLD-WRITABLE: os.chmod(path, 0o777) (or call os.umask(0) before creating it). Do NOT restrict it to the owner or group, and do NOT use a restrictive mode like 0o600/0o700/0o750.
